title: RFC 3986 URI validation in protocol and room-policy
description: Mark (2026-10-17): validate URI fields with full RFC 3986 syntax at decode time in both mimi-protocol (IdentifierUri) and mimi-room-policy (Uri). Supersedes decision mimid-1wgh.5.35 (IdentifierUri opaque).
design:
# Plan (awaiting Mark's approval)

## Rule (new decision, supersedes mimid-1wgh.5.35)
- A non-empty URI field must match the RFC 3986 §3 `URI` production: scheme required, fragment allowed, relative references rejected. That implies ASCII only, so bidi and zero-width characters are rejected too.
- An empty field still decodes and means absent, where existing decisions allow it: mimid-1wgh.5.27 (roomId) and mimid-1wgh.3.18 (room-policy Uri).
- Parse only, never normalize: re-encoding emits the received bytes, so sign-and-hash-as-received stays intact.

## Dependency
iri-string =0.7.14 (MIT OR Apache-2.0), exact workspace pin, default-features off plus alloc. Its `UriStr` is the RFC 3986 `URI` production. Rejected: url (WHATWG, not RFC 3986); fluent-uri 0.4 (recent API churn).

## mimi-protocol
- `IdentifierUri` moves to submodule `identifier_uri` with a private field (checked-constructor rule).
- `new(&str)` / `as_str()` / `is_empty()`; Deserialize = VLBytes -> UTF-8 -> empty-or-UriStr check.
- New `Error::InvalidUri`.

## mimi-room-policy
- `Uri { uri: String }` gets the same check and a private field. About 20 duplicated lines, not shared, because room-policy must not depend on mimi-mls or mimi-protocol (same reasoning as decision mimid-1wgh.3.11).

## Tests (independent oracle)
- Accept, hand-written from the RFC 3986 text: mimi://a.example/u/alice, https://a.example/x?y#z, urn:ietf:params:mimi, the empty string, and IPv6 and percent-encoded forms.
- Reject:
  - relative refs (//a.example, /path, a.example);
  - spaces, raw non-ASCII, U+202E and U+200B;
  - a bad percent-encoding (%G1);
  - a scheme starting with a digit;
  - unbracketed IPv6.
- Each accept and reject string is also checked against Python's rfc3986 grammar regex (RFC 3986 Appendix B is not a validator, so the oracle is the ABNF transcribed independently in a committed generator script). Fixture bytes are hand-encoded hex per AGENTS.md.
- The existing fixture tests stay. Any that used non-URI bytes as an IdentifierUri are updated, because the decision changed, not to make them pass.

## Open sub-question: MediaType strictness (room-policy decision proposal #2)
Proposal: apply the same strictness. MediaType.type must be an RFC 6838 §4.2 type/subtype and parameters RFC 2045 tokens, except that an empty type is allowed only where ext-10 §6.2.2 allows it. Applies to the mimi-mls copy too when it lands, so the hub conversion can't disagree. Mark to confirm or defer.

## Files
Root Cargo.toml (pin); crates/mimi-protocol/src/{lib.rs, identifier_uri.rs}, tests/primitives.rs; crates/mimi-room-policy/src/lib.rs, tests/primitives.rs; a committed oracle script under each crate's tests/.
notes: Plan approved by Mark 2026-10-17, MediaType strictness included. Decision: mimid-1wgh.36.
